title: Factory hardening follow-up: guard gaps, check override, trivial gate
request: Doug said yes to the factory hardening follow-up: (1) a trivial task must still be blocked by a recorded REJECT or CHANGES review; (2) refuse the check -- <cmd> override for every check; (3) close the push-to-a-protected-branch gap inside $( ), backticks, <( ), >( ), a subshell and a glued redirect; (4) stop the F check constructor crash; (5) a fail-closed cap on deep nesting in the guard; (6) README wording fixes plus the smoke-test result; (7) two test pins. Doug also confirmed by hand on 2026-11-04 that the hook ask prompted him in Auto mode, even when an allow rule matched.

criteria.text: F check <id> constructor, __proto__ and toString end with a plain No command for check error (exit 1): no TypeError, and no check record is written. Test first (RED on the old code).
criteria.evidence: cli.spec RED on the old code: 15 of 16 pass, 1 fails (a1-RED.txt). GREEN: 16 of 16 (a1-GREEN.txt). Names constructor, __proto__ and toString end with the plain No command error and write nothing.

criteria.text: F check <id> <name> -- <cmd> is refused for EVERY name (required, configured, or unknown): nothing runs and no record is written. The old test that expected a configured, not-required check to accept the override is replaced by its inverse. That is a deliberate decision by Doug (follow-up yes), not a weakened test. Test first.
criteria.evidence: cli.spec RED: 14 of 16 (a2-RED.txt), GREEN: 16 of 16 (a2-GREEN.txt). The override is refused for required, configured and unknown names. The old accept test is inverted on purpose (Doug said yes). The reviewer found the new test asserts more than the old one: status, three messages, no marker file, no log, no record.

criteria.text: A --trivial task whose latest code review is CHANGES or REJECT is NOT ready. A trivial task with an APPROVE, or with no review at all, still passes. Test first. factory/PIPELINE.md (two places) and the README line say so.
criteria.evidence: cli.spec RED: 16 of 17 (a3-RED.txt), GREEN: 17 of 17 (a3-GREEN.txt). Reviewer compared old and new gate logic on 1,885 review sequences: no difference for normal tasks; a trivial task is blocked only by a latest code review of CHANGES or REJECT. PIPELINE.md and the README say so.

criteria.text: The guard blocks a push to a protected branch inside $( ), backticks, <( ), >( ), a no-space subshell and with a redirect glued to the branch word. Controls stay true: a quoted ) before main is still blocked, and a feature-branch push inside $( ) is still allowed. Tests first: they fail on the old guard (I saw the old guard allow all six).
criteria.evidence: Guard spec RED on the old guard: 64 of 71 pass, 7 fail (guard-RED.txt). Final spec 76 of 76 on the installed guard (r1-guard-GREEN.txt). A push to a protected branch is blocked inside a substitution, backticks, process substitution, a subshell and with a glued redirect; controls stay true. Review round 1 found one regression (text glued after the closer); fixed by reading each push two ways (r1-guard-RED.txt shows it failing on the installed guard first). Re-check: 0 old-blocks-new-allows in about 80,000 inputs (r1-final-corpora.txt).

criteria.text: A command that nests more than 64 levels deep is BLOCKED by the guard (fail closed) with a plain reason, in well under a second. A command nested 60 deep is still checked normally. Real timings before and after are saved (before: 100 deep 216 ms, 250 deep 1039 ms, 400 deep 4270 ms).
criteria.evidence: Nest of 64 allowed, 65 blocked with a plain reason; 400 deep blocked in under 500 ms; 300 siblings allowed, 301 blocked; a line continuation cannot hide a wide nest; a protected delete at depth 60 is blocked for the right reason. timings.txt: depth 250 took 1402 ms before and 67 ms after; depth 400 took 4644 ms before and 68 ms after.

criteria.text: Two test pins: (a) a test that fails if the visited-set key stopped including the depth, and (b) a deeper timing test with a generous bound. Each is shown to fail when the thing it pins is broken (mutation run).
criteria.evidence: mutations.txt: dropping the depth from the visited key fails the pin test; removing the dedupe fails the two timing tests. r1-mutations.txt: 6 of 6 deliberate breakages (no union, no paren floor, no heredoc strip, tidy only, braces back in, joined text not measured) each fail the named test.

criteria.text: factory/README.md: the three wording fixes (the quoted-heredoc form needs a second EOF line; the quote-nesting limit also holds for a single-quoted word with a double quote; deep-nest timings vary by machine), the smoke-test result (dated 2026-11-04: Doug saw a prompt for both tests, so the hook ask prompted in Auto mode and beat an allow rule), and every known-limit line this task fixes is rewritten. Nothing else in the README changes meaning.
criteria.evidence: I read the README diff. Three wording fixes, the dated smoke-test result, the holes list (with the extra hole found by the re-check), the size limit with measured times (r1-cap-timing.txt), parens in quotes, and the corrected repair and resolve line (checked by running the CLI in a throwaway repo). The reviewer read it line by line; its one wrong-sentence finding was fixed in e83e613 and confirmed.

criteria.text: The guard was developed on a COPY and installed in one step: the installed factory/hooks/guard.mjs is byte-identical (sha256) to the copy that passed the specs, and node --check passes on it. The hook was never left in a broken state.
criteria.evidence: cmp shows the installed factory/hooks/guard.mjs is byte-identical to the copy that passed 76 of 76 specs (sha256 0444574b78a555b77f133035d8f8b24fcd83bf5c4ae16746a4dbe296aa15fd0b). node --check passes. It went in with one visible copy, a backup, a 5-point post-install check (5 of 5) and an automatic rollback; the output said INSTALLED-OK.

criteria.text: All required repo checks and the factory-specs check pass on the final commit, and a fresh independent reviewer approves it. Left alone and reported: git -C and git -c push or commit forms, the secret scan skip for those forms, the other documented limits.
criteria.evidence: All seven checks pass at e83e613: integrity, typecheck, lint, knip, build, unit, factory-specs. A fresh independent reviewer approved after one round of CHANGES. Left alone. Listed in the README: git -C and git -c forms, the quoted or escaped command word, 2>&1 before the remote, a remote-only push inside [ ], and the size limit. Reported to Doug in chat only, not in the README: the integrity scan does not see assert.equal style asserts, and factory .mjs files are not linted.

reviews.summary: Independent PLAN review: CHANGES, all points accepted in plan v2. The first push fix would have opened a hole (git push 2>/dev/null on main) and missed five forms; the cap must also bound width; the work copy needs .claude, .github and tools; keep the two specific override refusals.

Fresh reviewer: CHANGES. (1) REGRESSION, verified: a bare 'push' or 'push <remote>' on a protected branch, inside $( ) or backticks or an array subscript, with text glued after the closer, was blocked by the old guard and is allowed now. (2) The paren floor in parenDepth has no test. (3) New false positives: a protected name in ( ) [ ] { } after a push word in a commit message or PR body. (4) The cap does not bound run time for a very large body. (5) parenDepth counts parens inside quotes. (6) Some mutants survive. (7) README says F resolve crashes on a prototype key; it does not. CLI changes A1-A3 reviewed as fine.

Fresh reviewer: first pass CHANGES (7 findings, all fixed in e6fcced, 68eaf29, e83e613). Re-check APPROVE: 0 inputs the old guard blocked and the new one allows, across about 80,000 inputs (curated, fuzz against real bash, spec inputs); dropping braces and brackets opens no hole; all surviving mutants now fail a test. README delta e83e613 APPROVE.

history.summary: Read each push two ways (tidy and plain); a block from either wins. Zero regressions against the old guard on 729 curated pushes, 420 spec inputs, 166 normal commands, 374 depth cases and 3 fuzz seeds checked against real bash.

review1-push-regression.resolved: fixed in e6fcced and 68eaf29, verified by test and by corpus

history.summary: Added tests for the paren floor, for a heredoc body not counting toward the cap, for the push with glued text, and for braces and brackets. Six deliberate breakages of the guard are each caught by a test.

review1-test-gaps.resolved: fixed in e6fcced and 68eaf29, verified by test and by corpus

history.summary: Braces and brackets no longer cut the words of a push. Fewer prose false positives with no push missed. The README lists the ones that remain.

review1-false-positives.resolved: fixed in e6fcced and 68eaf29, verified by test and by corpus

history.summary: README: size limit with measured times, parens in quotes, the repair and resolve prototype-key wording checked by running the CLI. The comment on the cap no longer calls the counts cheap.

review1-doc-gaps.resolved: fixed in e6fcced and 68eaf29, verified by test and by corpus
